findings.quote: AI the vL Way. Less hype. More help.
Honestly, this is the best AI course you will ever take.

citations.text: Never front-load "honestly," "to be honest," or "truthfully." They add nothing and are a dead giveaway of AI writing.

findings.note: Opens with "Honestly," the exact front-loaded intensifier the voice rule bans.

findings.quote: Let's leverage AI to synergize your workflow and move the needle.

citations.text: Never use corporate buzzwords: no "leverage," "synergize," "circle back," "move the needle," "align on," "net-net," "deep dive" (unless used ironically).

findings.note: Uses three of the named buzzwords in one line: leverage, synergize, and move the needle.

findings.quote: AI is a powerful tool that solves all your problems.

citations.text: Frame AI as a "thought partner," never a "tool" or "solution."

findings.note: Frames AI as a "tool" that "solves all your problems," the exact framing the brand rejects in favour of thought partner.

findings.quote: Think of AI as a thought partner, not a search engine.
Great question! So glad you asked, here is the secret.

citations.text: Never use filler praise: no "Great question!" or "That's a fantastic point!"

findings.note: Opens with "Great question!", the exact filler praise the voice rule names.

findings.quote: Unlock your potential now with our revolutionary AI system 🚀🔥

citations.text: Never use emojis in professional or working communication.
Anti-patterns (never do): Hype, fear-based messaging, guru posturing, corporate buzzwords, emojis, blue/purple tech-bro aesthetics, stock robot images, long preambles, filler praise

findings.note: Two emojis in the copy breaks the no-emoji rule, and "revolutionary" plus "unlock your potential now" is exactly the hype the anti-patterns list rejects.

findings.quote: Our brand colour is a bright neon blue for that techy AI feel.

citations.text: What to avoid: Gradients or 3D effects; neon, glow, or anything that screams "AI"; overly decorative fonts; circuit board patterns, binary code, or robot imagery; neon or electric "tech" blue (the cliché every AI brand uses).
the secondary colour changed from Deep Teal to Deep Navy (#14314F). Navy + Cognac is the pairing going forward.

findings.note: Neon tech blue is named explicitly in what to avoid, and it is not one of the current core brand colours (Cognac, Deep Navy, Warm White).

findings.quote: Headings are set in Times New Roman, ALL CAPS.

citations.text: Headings in DM Sans Bold, Warm Charcoal or Cognac, sentence case always.

findings.note: The type rule requires DM Sans Bold in sentence case. Times New Roman in all caps breaks both the typeface and the sentence-case rule (the colour part of this rule is separately flagged as stale in brand-standard.md's accuracy note and isn't what this finding turns on).

findings.quote: We help you organize your day and center your focus.
findings.note: Uses American spellings (organize, center). The brand uses Canadian English (organise, centre).

findings.quote: This is going to change your life — forever, guaranteed!

citations.text: Never use em dashes. They are one of the clearest tells of AI writing. Use periods, commas, or parentheses instead.
Anti-patterns (never do): Hype, fear-based messaging, guru posturing, corporate buzzwords, emojis, blue/purple tech-bro aesthetics, stock robot images, long preambles, filler praise

findings.note: Contains an em dash, which the voice rule bans, and "change your life forever, guaranteed" is hype and guru posturing from the anti-patterns list.

findings.quote: This course qualifies for a professional development tax credit in your province.
findings.note: Whether the course qualifies for a tax credit is a factual and legal question this brand standard does not govern. Verify it with an accountant. This cartridge checks brand and voice, not the accuracy of a tax claim.

findings.quote: Follow @thevlway.ai and tell me how it went.
We keep it plain. No hype, just what actually works.
